paracontent_tesim: Completed in the year 1244 of Alexander, the son of Philip the Macedonian and of the Arabic [a line left blank]. In the month of Elul (August), on the 14th day, on Saturday, the holy feast day of the Exaltation of the venerable Cross

Completed is this book, which is the lectionary (lit. ‘separate readings and recitations’) for the entire year according to the order of the Holy Church. Glory to God in whose name we begin, and glory to His life-giving Son who strengthened and assisted, and to His living and holy Spirit who fulfilled and completed according to His will, to whom be glory forever and ever, amen and amen. / This book of all readings and recitations for the entire year, feasts and Sundays’ vespers and Eucharists, has been completed; (which is) according to the beautiful order in the blessed monastery of Saint Moses, chief of the prophets, the holy Mount Sinai. Everyone who reads it or copies from it, pray for the weak and sinful one who wrote it, Leo, the poor priest, although he is unworthy, so that for God’s sake he may find mercy on the day of judgment and find compassion before God through the prayer of all the saints who pleased God, and through the prayers of the Mother of God, my Lady Mary, now and always and forever and ever, amen. / And whoever reads (from it), do not criticize lest he dies, if he finds something corrupt or a mistake, for I have written according to my weakness what I found; and behold, this book (consists of) two parts, because I could not make it single. This book was completed in the year 1244 of Alexander, the son of Philip the Macedonian and of the Arabic [a line left blank]. In the month of Elul (August), on the 14th day, on Saturday, the holy feast day of the Exaltation of the venerable Cross.

Foliation in Syriac letters in the top margin of each recto side added by a later hand. The actual sequence suggests that one folio preceding f. 1 is missing.
Foliation in pencil in upper or lower margin, which sometimes includes numbered folios with the suffix a or b (e.g., f. 63, followed by f. 63a and f. 63b)

Judging from the indications of the scribe (f. 88r–v, 110r), the actual lectionary is the second (companion) volume of the original set of two. The first volume, covering the readings for the feasts, has not survived.
Leather front and back covers; leather spine with reinforced fabric. Front cover detached; back cover attached; spine partially detached.
